close_reason: Fixed in 84bcb9b. Both sites in src/email.rs (jmap_email_address_value:407, jmap_email_address_group_value:426) now use .expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible") matching the bc79c70 Pattern G canonical form. cargo build/test/clippy/fmt all clean.
description: src/email.rs:407,426 in jmap_email_address_value and jmap_email_address_group_value use serde_json::to_value(ea).unwrap_or(Value::Null) — the exact silent-serde-fallback antipattern that commit bc79c70 (Pattern G sweep, JMAP-tco1) replaced workspace-wide with .expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible"). The new code was added in commit e99c3dc (2026-05-13, four days AFTER bc79c70 on 2026-05-09) introducing two new instances of the very pattern the sweep eliminated. EmailAddress and EmailAddressGroup are both derive(Serialize) on plain data — to_value cannot fail. If it ever did, returning Value::Null would silently corrupt the apply_header_form output (a malformed From: header would surface as null in the field instead of a serverFail). Fix: replace .unwrap_or(Value::Null) with .expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible") at both sites. Trigger: any Email/get that requests a header:From:asAddresses or header:Sender:asGroupedAddresses property. Bad behavior: hypothetical serde failure surfaces as null in JSON wire output with no client signal.
title: Pattern G regression: apply_header_form swallows serde errors with unwrap_or(Value::Null)
